---- MODULE W4Od11m3p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Printers, Jobs, NoLeader

VARIABLES leader, term, crashed, queue, assigned, printed

vars == <<leader, term, crashed, queue, assigned, printed>>

\* A print-shop spooler cluster: one elected leader dispatches jobs from
\* the shared queue, holds them while printing, then marks them printed.
\* Leader election uses a monotonic term counter for failover. At most one
\* spooler can crash silently (the twist); a crashed leader stops making
\* progress until the survivors detect the failure and elect a fresh leader.
\* JobConservation checks that every job is always in exactly one of the
\* three life-cycle sets -- nothing is ever created, duplicated, or lost,
\* even across a silent crash and the ensuing failover.

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ term = 0
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ queue = Jobs
  /\ assigned = {}
  /\ printed = {}

Elect(p) ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ p \in Printers \ crashed
  /\ leader' = p
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, queue, assigned, printed>>

Crash(p) ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ p \in Printers
  /\ crashed' = {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, queue, assigned, printed>>

DetectFailure ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ leader \in crashed
  /\ leader' = NoLeader
  /\ queue' = queue \cup assigned
  /\ assigned' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, crashed, printed>>

Dispatch(j) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ leader \notin crashed
  /\ j \in queue
  /\ queue' = queue \ {j}
  /\ assigned' = assigned \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashed, printed>>

PrintJob(j) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ leader \notin crashed
  /\ j \in assigned
  /\ assigned' = assigned \ {j}
  /\ printed' = printed \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashed, queue>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Printers : Elect(p)
  \/ \E p \in Printers : Crash(p)
  \/ DetectFailure
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : Dispatch(j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : PrintJob(j)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(DetectFailure)
  /\ \A p \in Printers : WF_vars(Elect(p))
  /\ \A j \in Jobs : WF_vars(Dispatch(j)) /\ WF_vars(PrintJob(j))

JobConservation ==
  /\ queue \cup assigned \cup printed = Jobs
  /\ queue \cap assigned = {}
  /\ queue \cap printed = {}
  /\ assigned \cap printed = {}

AllJobsPrinted == <>(printed = Jobs)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
Printers = {p1, p2}
Jobs = {j1, j2}
NoLeader = NoLeader

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT JobConservation
PROPERTY AllJobsPrinted
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a small print shop, several networked print spoolers coordinate to service a shared queue of print jobs. Exactly one spooler acts as the leader at any time: it pulls jobs from the shared queue, holds them while the physical printer processes them, and then marks them printed. Leadership is established through a simple election mechanism with a monotonically increasing election term, and the cluster uses failover so that if the active leader goes silent, a surviving spooler takes over and resumes the queue.

The twist is that up to one spooler in the cluster can crash silently: it simply stops responding without sending any notification. If the crashed unit happens to be the current leader, any jobs it was holding become stuck until the remaining spoolers detect the failure and hand leadership to a healthy spooler, at which point those stuck jobs are returned to the shared queue so nothing is lost.

The full action set is: Elect(p), in which a spooler p that has not crashed takes over as leader (only possible when there is currently no leader) and bumps the election term; Crash(p), in which a spooler p silently fails (at most one spooler ever crashes in a run); DetectFailure, in which the surviving spooler cluster notices that the current leader has crashed and clears leadership, moving any jobs the crashed leader was holding back into the shared queue; Dispatch(j), in which the current non-crashed leader pulls job j out of the shared queue and holds it for printing; and PrintJob(j), in which the current non-crashed leader finishes printing job j and marks it printed.

Every job in the shop is always in exactly one of three places: waiting in the queue, held by the leader for printing, or printed. Jobs are never duplicated, never lost, and never appear from nowhere -- even the crash-and-failover path only ever moves a job back into the queue, it never drops it. Eventually, once the transient crash (if any) has been detected and a new leader elected, the whole backlog is worked off and every job reaches the printed state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every job is at all times in exactly one of the queue, the current leader's held set, or the printed set, so the total collection of jobs is conserved across leader crashes and failovers.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every job in the shop is eventually printed, even accounting for one silent leader crash and the resulting failover.

---- MODULE W4Od3m9p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Participants, MaxEpoch, Quorum, BatchAmount

VARIABLES epoch, acked, inflight, transferred, settled

vars == <<epoch, acked, inflight, transferred, settled>>

\* An interbank settlement batch is coordinated under an epoch-numbered
\* reconfiguration scheme: the coordinator can bump the epoch (dropping the
\* stale quorum) to route around a slow-but-not-failed member bank. Acks
\* travel through an in-flight buffer to model network delay, and any ack
\* that finally arrives tagged with an epoch older than the current one is
\* discarded as stale rather than counted toward the live quorum. The
\* actual money movement (Settle) is the irreversible action: it may only
\* fire while `settled` is still FALSE, and SettlementBounded checks that
\* the batch's funds are never moved more than the single BatchAmount --
\* i.e. the transfer really only ever happens once, even across epochs.

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ acked = {}
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ transferred = 0
  /\ settled = FALSE

Ack(p) ==
  /\ p \in Participants
  /\ p \notin acked
  /\ <<p, epoch>> \notin inflight
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {<<p, epoch>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, acked, transferred, settled>>

Deliver(p, e) ==
  /\ <<p, e>> \in inflight
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {<<p, e>>}
  /\ IF e = epoch
       THEN acked' = acked \cup {p}
       ELSE acked' = acked \* stale ack from a bygone epoch: discarded, not counted
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, transferred, settled>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ ~settled
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ Cardinality(acked) < Quorum \* only reconfigure while the current epoch is still stuck below quorum
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ acked' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, transferred, settled>>

Settle ==
  /\ ~settled
  /\ Cardinality(acked) >= Quorum
  /\ settled' = TRUE
  /\ transferred' = transferred + BatchAmount
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, acked, inflight>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Ack(p)
  \/ \E p \in Participants, e \in 1..MaxEpoch : Deliver(p, e)
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ Settle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SettlementBounded == transferred <= BatchAmount

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
Participants = {a, b, c}
MaxEpoch = 2
Quorum = 2
BatchAmount = 100

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SettlementBounded
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A batch of interbank payments must be settled by a small committee of member banks. The committee runs under an epoch-numbered reconfiguration scheme: the coordinator can advance to a new epoch, discarding the current tally of acknowledgements, whenever the quorum needed to approve the batch has not yet been reached. This lets the coordinator route around a member bank that is being slow -- not failed, just delayed -- without waiting on it forever.

Each bank's acknowledgement travels through a network buffer before it lands: a bank sends its ack (Ack), and only later does that ack actually arrive and get counted (Deliver). Because the coordinator may reconfigure to a new epoch while an old ack is still in flight, a slow bank's ack can arrive stamped with an epoch number that is no longer current. The system must discard such a stale ack rather than let it count toward the live quorum -- otherwise a batch could look approved on outdated evidence.

Once quorum is reached in the current epoch, the coordinator executes the actual money movement for the batch (Settle). This is the irreversible action: real funds move between the member banks' accounts, and it must never be allowed to happen more than once for the same batch, no matter how many epochs the committee cycled through to get there.

The full action set is: Ack(p), where member bank p places its acknowledgement of the current epoch into the in-flight buffer; Deliver(p, e), where a previously sent ack from bank p tagged with epoch e finally arrives -- it is counted toward the live quorum if e matches the current epoch, and silently discarded as stale otherwise; Reconfigure, where the coordinator advances to a new epoch and clears the current tally because quorum has not yet been reached (used to work around a slow bank); and Settle, where the coordinator, having observed quorum in the current epoch, executes the batch's fund transfer exactly once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the batch's settlement funds are never transferred more than the single authorized BatchAmount, so the irreversible settlement action can never effectively execute twice, even though the committee may reconfigure through several epochs and stale acknowledgements from a slow bank may arrive after the fact.

---- MODULE W4Od5m8p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Lobbies, Cap, NoP

VARIABLES pool, seated, coarseHolder, fineHolder, inflight, misordered

vars == <<pool, seated, coarseHolder, fineHolder, inflight, misordered>>

\* A matchmaker seats waiting players into lobbies using hierarchical
\* locking: a player first grabs the single coarse "matchmaker" lock, then
\* a fine per-lobby lock, before its join message can be seated. Join
\* messages travel through an unordered in-flight set. Normally a fine
\* lock is only released after its own join has been delivered, but the
\* network can, at most once in a run, reorder a fine-lock release ahead
\* of its own pending join (the twist); SeatOne re-checks fine lock
\* ownership at delivery time and drops a message whose lock has since
\* moved on, so that one reordering glitch never seats a player twice.
\* PlayerConservation checks that every player is always in exactly one
\* place -- the waiting pool or exactly one lobby's seats -- so players
\* are never duplicated or dropped as they move through the lock chain.

Init ==
  /\ pool = Players
  /\ seated = [l \in Lobbies |-> {}]
  /\ coarseHolder = NoP
  /\ fineHolder = [l \in Lobbies |-> NoP]
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ misordered = FALSE

AcquireCoarse(p) ==
  /\ p \in pool
  /\ coarseHolder = NoP
  /\ coarseHolder' = p
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seated, fineHolder, inflight, misordered>>

AcquireFine(p, l) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = p
  /\ p \in pool \* only a still-waiting player may pursue a lobby seat -- a seated player can't grab a second one
  /\ fineHolder[l] = NoP
  /\ \A l2 \in Lobbies : fineHolder[l2] # p \* a player only opens one fine lock at a time
  /\ Cardinality(seated[l]) < Cap
  /\ fineHolder' = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![l] = p]
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {<<p, l>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seated, coarseHolder, misordered>>

SeatOne(p, l) ==
  /\ <<p, l>> \in inflight
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {<<p, l>>}
  /\ IF fineHolder[l] = p
       THEN /\ seated' = [seated EXCEPT ![l] = seated[l] \cup {p}]
            /\ pool' = pool \ {p}
       ELSE /\ seated' = seated \* fine lock moved on before this reordered join landed: stale, dropped
            /\ pool' = pool
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, misordered>>

\* A fine lock is released after its own join has been delivered (the safe,
\* ordinary path). At most once in a run, the network can instead reorder
\* the release message ahead of the still-pending join -- that single
\* glitch is what makes SeatOne's stale-drop branch reachable.
ReleaseFine(p, l) ==
  /\ fineHolder[l] = p
  /\ fineHolder' = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![l] = NoP]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seated, coarseHolder, inflight>>
  /\ \/ /\ <<p, l>> \notin inflight
        /\ UNCHANGED misordered
     \/ /\ <<p, l>> \in inflight
        /\ ~misordered
        /\ misordered' = TRUE

ReleaseCoarse(p) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = p
  /\ \A l \in Lobbies : fineHolder[l] # p \* hierarchical discipline: can't drop the coarse lock while a fine lock under it is still held
  /\ coarseHolder' = NoP
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seated, fineHolder, inflight, misordered>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Players : AcquireCoarse(p)
  \/ \E p \in Players, l \in Lobbies : AcquireFine(p, l)
  \/ \E p \in Players, l \in Lobbies : SeatOne(p, l)
  \/ \E p \in Players, l \in Lobbies : ReleaseFine(p, l)
  \/ \E p \in Players : ReleaseCoarse(p)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Players : AcquireCoarse(p))
  /\ SF_vars(\E p \in Players, l \in Lobbies : AcquireFine(p, l))
  /\ SF_vars(\E p \in Players, l \in Lobbies : SeatOne(p, l))
  /\ SF_vars(\E p \in Players, l \in Lobbies : ReleaseFine(p, l))
  /\ SF_vars(\E p \in Players : ReleaseCoarse(p))

PlayerConservation ==
  /\ pool \cup UNION {seated[l] : l \in Lobbies} = Players
  /\ \A l1, l2 \in Lobbies : l1 # l2 => seated[l1] \cap seated[l2] = {}
  /\ \A l \in Lobbies : pool \cap seated[l] = {}

EventuallyAllSeated == <>(pool = {})

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
Players = {pl1, pl2, pl3}
Lobbies = {l1, l2}
Cap = 2
NoP = NoP

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PlayerConservation
PROPERTY EventuallyAllSeated
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats waiting players into lobbies using a hierarchical locking scheme: a player must first grab the single coarse "matchmaker" lock that governs the whole matching round, and only then may it grab a fine-grained lock on the specific lobby it wants to join. Once a player holds both locks it sends a join message announcing that it should be seated in that lobby, releases the fine lock, and finally releases the coarse lock so another waiting player can take a turn.

The twist is that join messages are delivered through an unordered network buffer, so they can arrive out of order relative to lock releases: a player might release its fine lock on a lobby before its own earlier join message has actually been delivered, and by the time that message does arrive, the fine lock on that lobby may already belong to someone else. The matchmaker handles this by re-checking, at delivery time, whether the fine lock is still held by the sender; if it is not, the stale join message is silently dropped instead of seating the wrong player or seating someone twice.

The full action set is: AcquireCoarse(p), where a still-waiting player p grabs the coarse matchmaker lock (only possible while no one else holds it); AcquireFine(p, l), where the current coarse-lock holder p, provided it is still waiting to be seated, grabs the fine lock on lobby l (only possible if that lobby's fine lock is free, the lobby is not yet full, and p is not already holding a different lobby's fine lock) and sends its join message; SeatOne(p, l), where a previously sent join message from player p for lobby l is delivered -- seating p in l only if p still holds l's fine lock at that moment, and otherwise dropping the stale message; ReleaseFine(p, l), where p releases its fine lock on lobby l; and ReleaseCoarse(p), where p releases the coarse lock, which is only allowed once p is not holding any fine lock, preserving the coarse-then-fine locking hierarchy.

Every player in the matchmaking pool is at all times in exactly one place: still waiting in the pool, or seated in exactly one lobby. No player is ever created, duplicated across two lobbies, or lost, no matter how the join and release messages get reordered. Given that the matchmaker keeps cycling the coarse lock among waiting players, every waiting player is eventually seated in some lobby.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every player is at all times in exactly one of the waiting pool or exactly one lobby's seated set, so players are conserved -- never duplicated into two lobbies and never lost -- even when join and lock-release messages are delivered out of order.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every player waiting in the pool is eventually seated in some lobby, so the pool eventually becomes empty.

---- MODULE W4Od6m6p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Floors, NoCar, NoFloor

VARIABLES pendingCalls, leaseHolder, servingFloor, crashed

vars == <<pendingCalls, leaseHolder, servingFloor, crashed>>

\* An elevator bank dispatches cars to floor calls using lease-based
\* ownership: a car must hold the current lease for a floor before it may
\* open its doors there. A granted-but-unopened lease can later be
\* reclaimed by an abstract timeout, which is how the bank recovers when
\* the car it assigned crashes silently before ever starting service (the
\* twist) -- at most one car can crash, and a crashed car can never again
\* be granted a lease or open a door. DoorAuthorization checks that a
\* car's door is only ever open for a floor whose lease it currently and
\* legitimately holds, i.e. no unauthorized or stale participant ever
\* opens a door.

Init ==
  /\ pendingCalls = {}
  /\ leaseHolder = [f \in Floors |-> NoCar]
  /\ servingFloor = [c \in Cars |-> NoFloor]
  /\ crashed = {}

PlaceCall(f) ==
  /\ f \notin pendingCalls
  /\ leaseHolder[f] = NoCar
  /\ pendingCalls' = pendingCalls \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, servingFloor, crashed>>

GrantLease(c, f) ==
  /\ c \notin crashed
  /\ f \in pendingCalls
  /\ leaseHolder[f] = NoCar
  /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![f] = c]
  /\ pendingCalls' = pendingCalls \ {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<servingFloor, crashed>>

OpenDoor(c, f) ==
  /\ c \notin crashed
  /\ servingFloor[c] = NoFloor
  /\ leaseHolder[f] = c
  /\ servingFloor' = [servingFloor EXCEPT ![c] = f]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingCalls, leaseHolder, crashed>>

CloseDoor(c) ==
  /\ servingFloor[c] # NoFloor
  /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![servingFloor[c]] = NoCar]
  /\ servingFloor' = [servingFloor EXCEPT ![c] = NoFloor]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingCalls, crashed>>

\* Abstract timeout: reclaims a lease that was granted but never opened
\* (e.g. its car crashed before starting service). Never fires while some
\* car's door is actually open for the floor, so a live service is never
\* yanked out from under it.
Reclaim(f) ==
  /\ leaseHolder[f] # NoCar
  /\ \A c \in Cars : servingFloor[c] # f
  /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![f] = NoCar]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingCalls, servingFloor, crashed>>

Crash(c) ==
  /\ Cardinality(crashed) = 0
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingCalls, leaseHolder, servingFloor>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Floors : PlaceCall(f)
  \/ \E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : GrantLease(c, f)
  \/ \E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : OpenDoor(c, f)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : CloseDoor(c)
  \/ \E f \in Floors : Reclaim(f)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Crash(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DoorAuthorization ==
  \A c \in Cars : servingFloor[c] # NoFloor => leaseHolder[servingFloor[c]] = c

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
Cars = {c1, c2}
Floors = {f1, f2, f3}
NoCar = NoCar
NoFloor = NoFloor

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DoorAuthorization
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A bank of elevator cars in a skyscraper serves floor calls using a lease-based dispatch scheme. When a passenger presses a call button, the floor's call becomes pending; the dispatcher then grants exactly one car a lease on that floor, and only the car currently holding a floor's lease is allowed to open its doors there. Once a car finishes serving a floor it closes its doors and releases the lease, freeing the floor for a fresh call.

The twist is that one car in the bank can crash silently at any point: it simply stops responding, and from that moment on it can never be granted a new lease and can never open a door again. If the dispatcher happens to have granted the crashed car a lease on a floor it never got around to opening -- the crash struck between the grant and the door opening -- that lease would otherwise sit there forever, permanently blocking the floor from being reassigned. To recover, the bank's dispatcher runs an abstract timeout that can reclaim any lease that has been granted but not yet opened, freeing the floor to be leased to a different, healthy car. The timeout never reclaims a lease while a car's door is actually open for that floor, so a service already underway is never interrupted.

The full action set is: PlaceCall(f), where a passenger presses the call button for floor f, adding it to the pending set (only if it is not already pending and no car currently holds its lease); GrantLease(c, f), where the dispatcher assigns a pending floor call f to a car c that has not crashed, handing c the lease and clearing the call from the pending set; OpenDoor(c, f), where car c, which must not have crashed and must currently hold floor f's lease, opens its doors to serve f; CloseDoor(c), where car c, which currently has its doors open for some floor, closes them and releases that floor's lease; Reclaim(f), where the dispatcher's timeout reclaims floor f's lease because it was granted but no car's doors are currently open for f, making the floor available again; and Crash(c), where car c silently crashes (at most one car in the bank ever crashes in a run).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a car's doors are open for a floor only while that car currently and legitimately holds that floor's lease, so no unauthorized car and no car acting on a stale, already-reclaimed lease can ever open its doors -- even when the car originally granted the lease has crashed silently.

---- MODULE W4Od17m9p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bags, Slots, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, confirmed, pending, waiting, delivered

vars == <<epoch, confirmed, pending, waiting, delivered>>

\* An airport baggage router assigns bags to physical carousel slots under
\* an epoch-numbered reconfiguration scheme: a bag first sends a tentative
\* request for a slot, and only a later, deliberately slow confirmation
\* step actually grants it (the scanner that confirms is slow but never
\* fails -- the twist -- so a sent confirmation is merely delayed, never
\* lost). If the router reconfigures to a new routing epoch, any request
\* still tagged with the old epoch becomes stale and must be rejected and
\* retried. SlotNotDoubleAllocated checks that the confirmed-allocation
\* relation never lets two different bags hold the same slot at once.

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ confirmed = {}
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ waiting = Bags
  /\ delivered = {}

RequestSlot(b, s) ==
  /\ b \in waiting
  /\ \A b2 \in Bags : <<b2, s>> \notin confirmed
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {<<b, s, epoch>>}
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, confirmed, delivered>>

\* The scanner's confirmation: slow (can be delayed arbitrarily by other
\* interleaved actions) but never fails, so it always eventually fires once
\* its request is still valid and the slot is still free.
ConfirmSlot(b, s, e) ==
  /\ <<b, s, e>> \in pending
  /\ e = epoch
  /\ \A b2 \in Bags : <<b2, s>> \notin confirmed
  /\ confirmed' = confirmed \cup {<<b, s>>}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {<<b, s, e>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, waiting, delivered>>

RejectStale(b, s, e) ==
  /\ <<b, s, e>> \in pending
  /\ \/ e # epoch
     \/ \E b2 \in Bags : b2 # b /\ <<b2, s>> \in confirmed
  /\ pending' = pending \ {<<b, s, e>>}
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, confirmed, delivered>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<confirmed, pending, waiting, delivered>>

Deliver(b) ==
  /\ \E s \in Slots :
       /\ <<b, s>> \in confirmed
       /\ confirmed' = confirmed \ {<<b, s>>}
  /\ delivered' = delivered \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pending, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bags, s \in Slots : RequestSlot(b, s)
  \/ \E b \in Bags, s \in Slots, e \in 1..MaxEpoch : ConfirmSlot(b, s, e)
  \/ \E b \in Bags, s \in Slots, e \in 1..MaxEpoch : RejectStale(b, s, e)
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E b \in Bags : Deliver(b)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A b \in Bags : WF_vars(\E s \in Slots : RequestSlot(b, s))
  /\ \A b \in Bags : WF_vars(\E s \in Slots, e \in 1..MaxEpoch : ConfirmSlot(b, s, e))
  /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Bags, s \in Slots, e \in 1..MaxEpoch : RejectStale(b, s, e))

SlotNotDoubleAllocated ==
  \A s \in Slots : \A b1, b2 \in Bags :
    (<<b1, s>> \in confirmed /\ <<b2, s>> \in confirmed) => b1 = b2

Allocated(b) == \E s \in Slots : <<b, s>> \in confirmed

EventualAllocation == <>(\A b \in Bags : Allocated(b) \/ b \in delivered)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
Bags = {b1, b2}
Slots = {s1, s2, s3}
MaxEpoch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SlotNotDoubleAllocated
PROPERTY EventualAllocation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport baggage router assigns arriving bags to physical slots on a sorting carousel, using an epoch-numbered reconfiguration scheme for the routing topology. A bag first sends a tentative request naming a slot it would like; only later does a scanner actually confirm the request and grant the bag that slot. The scanner that performs confirmation is slow -- it can take an arbitrarily long time to get around to a given confirmation -- but it is never allowed to fail outright, so a sent confirmation is only ever delayed, never dropped or lost.

The router occasionally reconfigures the carousel's routing topology, advancing to a new epoch. Any request still carrying an old epoch number is stale once that happens and must be rejected; the affected bag simply goes back to waiting and issues a fresh request under the current epoch. Because the confirming scanner double-checks, at confirmation time, that the requested slot is still unclaimed, two bags racing for the same slot can never both end up holding it: whichever confirmation lands first wins, and the other bag's now-stale request is rejected and retried.

The full action set is: RequestSlot(b, s), where a still-waiting bag b sends a tentative request for slot s, provided no bag currently holds s; ConfirmSlot(b, s, e), where the slow scanner confirms bag b's pending request for slot s tagged with epoch e -- only valid if e is still the current epoch and s is still unclaimed, and it is this action that actually grants the allocation; RejectStale(b, s, e), where a pending request is discarded because its epoch has been superseded by a reconfiguration or because another bag's confirmation beat it to slot s, sending b back to the waiting pool to try again; Reconfigure, where the router advances the routing topology to a new epoch, invalidating any request still tagged with the old one; and Deliver(b), where a bag b that currently holds a confirmed slot is unloaded at its destination, freeing that slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the confirmed-allocation relation never assigns the same slot to two different bags at once, so no slot is ever double allocated, even while multiple bags race to request it and the router reconfigures the routing epoch mid-race.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bag is eventually either holding a confirmed slot or already delivered, so no bag waits forever despite the scanner's slowness and the router's epoch reconfigurations.

---- MODULE W4Od18m9p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Locks, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, wiped, wipeGeneration, pending, credentialsCleared

vars == <<epoch, wiped, wipeGeneration, pending, credentialsCleared>>

\* A smart-home door lock network is coordinated by a hub under an
\* epoch-numbered reconfiguration scheme (the hub periodically rekeys the
\* network, advancing the epoch). The hub can issue a single irreversible
\* network-wide credential wipe order; the order travels as an in-flight
\* message tagged with the epoch it was issued in, and the network
\* (the twist) can deliver it late -- possibly after a reconfiguration has
\* already moved the epoch on, in which case it must be discarded as
\* stale rather than committed. WipeAtMostOnce checks that the wipe is
\* actually committed at most once, and that no lock ever shows cleared
\* credentials before the network-wide wipe has genuinely committed.

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ wiped = FALSE
  /\ wipeGeneration = 0
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ credentialsCleared = {}

IssueWipe ==
  /\ ~wiped
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {epoch}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, wiped, wipeGeneration, credentialsCleared>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wiped, wipeGeneration, pending, credentialsCleared>>

\* Commits the irreversible wipe -- only for an in-flight order whose tag
\* still matches the live epoch, and only while no wipe has committed yet.
CommitWipe(e) ==
  /\ e \in pending
  /\ e = epoch
  /\ ~wiped
  /\ wiped' = TRUE
  /\ wipeGeneration' = wipeGeneration + 1
  /\ pending' = pending \ {e}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credentialsCleared>>

\* A reordered wipe order arrives after the network has moved on (its
\* epoch tag no longer matches) or after the wipe has already committed:
\* it is dropped rather than acted upon.
DiscardStale(e) ==
  /\ e \in pending
  /\ \/ e # epoch
     \/ wiped
  /\ pending' = pending \ {e}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, wiped, wipeGeneration, credentialsCleared>>

ApplyToLock(l) ==
  /\ wiped
  /\ l \notin credentialsCleared
  /\ credentialsCleared' = credentialsCleared \cup {l}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, wiped, wipeGeneration, pending>>

Next ==
  \/ IssueWipe
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E e \in 1..MaxEpoch : CommitWipe(e)
  \/ \E e \in 1..MaxEpoch : DiscardStale(e)
  \/ \E l \in Locks : ApplyToLock(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WipeAtMostOnce ==
  /\ wipeGeneration <= 1
  /\ \A l \in Locks : l \in credentialsCleared => wipeGeneration >= 1

====

CONSTANTS
Locks = {l1, l2, l3}
MaxEpoch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT WipeAtMostOnce
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A smart-home door lock network is coordinated by a central hub under an epoch-numbered reconfiguration scheme: the hub periodically rekeys the whole network, advancing to a new epoch, to rotate credentials and drop any locks that should no longer trust the old key material. Separately, the hub has the ability to issue a single, irreversible network-wide credential wipe -- an emergency action that permanently invalidates every lock's stored credentials, forcing them all to be re-enrolled from scratch. This wipe order is meant to happen at most once.

The wipe order does not take effect instantly: it travels through the home network as a message tagged with the epoch it was issued in. The twist is that this network can reorder and delay messages, so the wipe order can arrive late -- possibly after the hub has already rekeyed the network into a new epoch. When that happens, the stale order (still carrying the old epoch's tag) must be recognized as no longer valid and discarded rather than acted on, so a late, out-of-date wipe order can never sneak through and trigger a second, spurious wipe.

The full action set is: IssueWipe, where the hub sends the single irreversible wipe order into the network, tagged with the current epoch (only possible if no wipe has committed yet and no wipe order is already in flight); Reconfigure, where the hub advances the network to a new epoch, rekeying the system; CommitWipe(e), where an in-flight wipe order tagged with epoch e is actually applied -- only valid if e still matches the current live epoch and no wipe has committed before; DiscardStale(e), where an in-flight wipe order tagged with epoch e is dropped because either its epoch no longer matches the current one or a wipe has already committed; and ApplyToLock(l), where an individual lock l, having learned that the network-wide wipe has committed, clears its own locally stored credentials.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the irreversible network-wide credential wipe commits at most once, and no lock ever shows cleared credentials unless that single wipe has genuinely committed -- even though the wipe order can be delayed and delivered after the network has since reconfigured to a new epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od13m5p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS InstanceA, InstanceB, Requesters

Voters == InstanceA \cup InstanceB

VARIABLES holders, requesting, votes, done

vars == <<holders, requesting, votes, done>>

\* Two independent vending-machine instances (InstanceA and InstanceB)
\* share a single physical resource pool (e.g. one coin hopper). Before a
\* requesting machine may take exclusive hold of the pool it must win a
\* quorum vote from strictly more than half of ALL voters across BOTH
\* instances combined (the twist) -- neither instance's members alone are
\* numerous enough to reach that quorum by themselves, so genuine
\* cross-instance agreement is required, not just local consensus.
\* MutualExclusion checks that the shared pool is never held by more than
\* one machine at a time.

Init ==
  /\ holders = {}
  /\ requesting = {}
  /\ votes = [m \in Requesters |-> {}]
  /\ done = {}

\* Only one candidate at a time is allowed to solicit votes -- this keeps
\* the quorum voters from ever splitting their support between two
\* simultaneously-open requests, which would otherwise let each request
\* get stuck forever with only its own instance's votes.
Request(m) ==
  /\ m \in Requesters
  /\ m \notin requesting
  /\ m \notin holders
  /\ m \notin done
  /\ requesting = {}
  /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {m}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, done>>

Vote(v, m) ==
  /\ v \in Voters
  /\ m \in Requesters
  /\ m \in requesting
  /\ v \notin votes[m]
  /\ \A m2 \in Requesters : (m2 \in requesting /\ m2 # m) => v \notin votes[m2]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m] = votes[m] \cup {v}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, requesting, done>>

Grant(m) ==
  /\ m \in Requesters
  /\ m \in requesting
  /\ holders = {}
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes[m]) > Cardinality(Voters)
  /\ holders' = holders \cup {m}
  /\ requesting' = requesting \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, done>>

Release(m) ==
  /\ m \in holders
  /\ holders' = holders \ {m}
  /\ done' = done \cup {m}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED requesting

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Requesters : Request(m)
  \/ \E v \in Voters, m \in Requesters : Vote(v, m)
  \/ \E m \in Requesters : Grant(m)
  \/ \E m \in Requesters : Release(m)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A m \in Requesters : WF_vars(Request(m))
  /\ \A v \in Voters, m \in Requesters : SF_vars(Vote(v, m))
  /\ \A m \in Requesters : SF_vars(Grant(m))
  /\ \A m \in Requesters : SF_vars(Release(m))

MutualExclusion == Cardinality(holders) <= 1

EventualService == <>(\A m \in Requesters : m \in done)

====
nl:
Two independent vending-machine instances share a single physical resource pool -- for example, one shared coin hopper that both instances' machines draw change from. Because the pool is genuinely shared across the two otherwise-independent instances, exclusive access to it is arbitrated by quorum voting across every machine in both instances combined, not by either instance managing it locally.

A machine that wants the pool opens a request, but only one request may be open for voting at a time -- this keeps the voting body from ever splitting its attention between two competing candidates, which would otherwise let each one get permanently stuck with support from only its own instance. Once a request is open, any machine in either instance may cast a vote for it, and a machine only ever backs one open request at a time. The requesting machine is granted exclusive hold of the pool only once it has collected votes from strictly more than half of all the voters across both instances combined -- a threshold that neither instance's own membership is large enough to reach by itself, so real cross-instance agreement is required every time. Once the holding machine is done, it releases the pool, clearing the way for the next request.

The full action set is: Request(m), where machine m opens a request for the shared pool, provided no other request is currently open, m is not already holding or done, and it starts with an empty vote tally; Vote(v, m), where a machine v (from either instance) casts a vote in favor of the currently open request from m, provided v has not already voted for a different currently-open request; Grant(m), where request m is granted exclusive hold of the pool once its vote tally exceeds half of all voters across both instances and the pool is currently free; and Release(m), where the machine m currently holding the pool gives it up, marking itself done.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared pool is held by at most one machine at a time, so the two independent instances can never simultaneously use it, no matter how the quorum votes are cast.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every machine that requests the shared pool is eventually granted it and completes its use, so no requester waits forever for cross-instance quorum.

---- MODULE W4Od18m8p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Guests, Doors, MaxGuests, NoG

VARIABLES coarseHolder, fineHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors, ackInflight

vars == <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

\* A smart-home door lock network issues temporary guest credentials using
\* hierarchical locking: a single coarse home-wide lock admits at most one
\* guest-issuance transaction at a time, and reserves the transaction's
\* capacity slot immediately; a fine per-door lock is then taken briefly
\* while the credential is written into each door's local memory. Each
\* door's write-completion acknowledgement travels through an unordered
\* buffer, so acks can be delivered out of order or after the issuance
\* that sent them has already been cancelled (the twist); ProcessAck only
\* credits a door's write toward the CURRENT coarse holder, so a stale ack
\* from a cancelled issuance can never be misattributed. CapacityBounded
\* checks that the number of active guest credentials never exceeds the
\* home's configured limit.

Init ==
  /\ coarseHolder = NoG
  /\ fineHolder = [d \in Doors |-> NoG]
  /\ activeGuests = {}
  /\ writtenDoors = {}
  /\ ackInflight = {}

\* Reserves the capacity slot as soon as an issuance transaction begins --
\* this is the single point that enforces the bound, regardless of how
\* the per-door writes and their acks are later interleaved or reordered.
StartIssue(g) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = NoG
  /\ g \notin activeGuests
  /\ Cardinality(activeGuests) < MaxGuests
  /\ coarseHolder' = g
  /\ activeGuests' = activeGuests \cup {g}
  /\ writtenDoors' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineHolder, ackInflight>>

AcquireFineWrite(g, d) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = g
  /\ fineHolder[d] = NoG
  /\ d \notin writtenDoors
  /\ fineHolder' = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![d] = g]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

ReleaseFineAndAck(g, d) ==
  /\ fineHolder[d] = g
  /\ fineHolder' = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![d] = NoG]
  /\ ackInflight' = ackInflight \cup {<<g, d>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors>>

\* A door's write ack arrives, possibly late or out of order. It only
\* counts toward completion if the sender is still the live coarse
\* holder -- a reordered ack for a since-cancelled issuance is dropped.
ProcessAck(g, d) ==
  /\ <<g, d>> \in ackInflight
  /\ ackInflight' = ackInflight \ {<<g, d>>}
  /\ IF coarseHolder = g
       THEN writtenDoors' = writtenDoors \cup {d}
       ELSE writtenDoors' = writtenDoors
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, activeGuests>>

FinishIssue(g) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = g
  /\ writtenDoors = Doors
  /\ coarseHolder' = NoG
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

\* An issuance can be abandoned before every door has been written (e.g.
\* the guest declined). Its capacity slot is released immediately, but
\* any of its acks already in flight are left untouched -- they will
\* later be safely dropped by ProcessAck's staleness check.
CancelIssue(g) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = g
  /\ writtenDoors # Doors
  /\ coarseHolder' = NoG
  /\ activeGuests' = activeGuests \ {g}
  /\ fineHolder' = [d \in Doors |-> IF fineHolder[d] = g THEN NoG ELSE fineHolder[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

Revoke(g) ==
  /\ g \in activeGuests
  /\ coarseHolder # g
  /\ activeGuests' = activeGuests \ {g}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

Next ==
  \/ \E g \in Guests : StartIssue(g)
  \/ \E g \in Guests, d \in Doors : AcquireFineWrite(g, d)
  \/ \E g \in Guests, d \in Doors : ReleaseFineAndAck(g, d)
  \/ \E g \in Guests, d \in Doors : ProcessAck(g, d)
  \/ \E g \in Guests : FinishIssue(g)
  \/ \E g \in Guests : CancelIssue(g)
  \/ \E g \in Guests : Revoke(g)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityBounded == Cardinality(activeGuests) <= MaxGuests

====

CONSTANTS
Guests = {g1, g2, g3}
Doors = {d1, d2}
MaxGuests = 2
NoG = NoG

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityBounded
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A smart-home door lock network issues temporary guest access credentials across all of a home's doors at once, using a hierarchical locking scheme. A single coarse, home-wide lock admits only one guest-issuance transaction at a time and immediately reserves that transaction's slot against the home's configured limit on simultaneously active guest credentials. Once admitted, the transaction takes a fine-grained lock on each individual door in turn to write the new credential into that door's local memory, then releases the door's lock and sends an acknowledgement back to the hub confirming the write.

The twist is that these per-door write acknowledgements travel through an unordered network buffer, so they can arrive late or out of order -- and in particular, an acknowledgement can still be in flight when its own issuance transaction gets cancelled (for example, if the guest declines partway through setup). The hub handles this by only crediting an acknowledgement toward an issuance's progress if the sender is still the currently active coarse-lock holder; a stale acknowledgement that arrives after its issuance has already been cancelled is simply dropped rather than mistakenly counted.

The full action set is: StartIssue(g), where guest g's issuance transaction takes the coarse lock, provided no other issuance is in progress and the home is under its configured limit on active credentials -- this is the point where g's capacity slot is reserved; AcquireFineWrite(g, d), where the current coarse-lock holder g takes the fine lock on door d to write g's credential there; ReleaseFineAndAck(g, d), where g releases door d's fine lock and sends the write's acknowledgement into the network; ProcessAck(g, d), where a previously sent acknowledgement from g for door d is delivered -- it counts toward g's progress only if g is still the current coarse-lock holder, and is otherwise dropped as stale; FinishIssue(g), where g's transaction completes once every door has been written, releasing the coarse lock; CancelIssue(g), where g's transaction is abandoned before every door was written, releasing the coarse lock and g's reserved capacity slot immediately; and Revoke(g), where a guest g with an already-active credential has it revoked, freeing its capacity slot for reuse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of simultaneously active guest credentials never exceeds the home's configured limit, no matter how the per-door write acknowledgements are delayed, reordered, or rendered stale by a cancelled issuance.

---- MODULE W4Od10m8p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Subway signalling block system with hierarchical locking: a train first
\* claims a coarse zone-capacity token before it may claim fine-grained
\* per-block locks inside that zone. The invariant guards conservation of
\* movement-authority capacity: a block may only be occupied while the
\* occupying train legitimately holds the matching zone token, so capacity
\* is never manufactured (occupy without authority) nor stranded (authority
\* released while blocks still depend on it).

CONSTANTS Trains, Z1Blocks, Z2Blocks, Z1Tokens, Z2Tokens

Blocks == Z1Blocks \cup Z2Blocks
Tokens == Z1Tokens \cup Z2Tokens

\* A token backs a block only if both belong to the same signalling zone.
SameZone(tok, b) == \/ (tok \in Z1Tokens /\ b \in Z1Blocks)
                     \/ (tok \in Z2Tokens /\ b \in Z2Blocks)

VARIABLES tokenHolder, blockOcc, trainToken, trainBlocks, usedBlocks, slow

vars == <<tokenHolder, blockOcc, trainToken, trainBlocks, usedBlocks, slow>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ tokenHolder \in [Tokens -> Trains \cup {"free"}]
  /\ blockOcc \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {"free"}]
  /\ trainToken \in [Trains -> Tokens \cup {"none"}]
  /\ trainBlocks \in [Trains -> SUBSET Blocks]
  /\ usedBlocks \in [Trains -> 0..2]
  /\ slow \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ tokenHolder = [tok \in Tokens |-> "free"]
  /\ blockOcc = [b \in Blocks |-> "free"]
  /\ trainToken = [t \in Trains |-> "none"]
  /\ trainBlocks = [t \in Trains |-> {}]
  /\ usedBlocks = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
  /\ slow = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]

\* A slow train is granted advance clearance for one extra block per zone
\* visit so reduced speed does not stall the corridor -- the twist changes a
\* real guard (MaxBlocksFor), it is not just narrative flavor.
MaxBlocksFor(t) == IF slow[t] THEN 2 ELSE 1

\* Coarse lock: claim the zone-level capacity token.
AcquireZone(t, tok) ==
  /\ trainToken[t] = "none"
  /\ trainBlocks[t] = {}
  /\ tokenHolder[tok] = "free"
  /\ tokenHolder' = [tokenHolder EXCEPT ![tok] = t]
  /\ trainToken' = [trainToken EXCEPT ![t] = tok]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockOcc, trainBlocks, usedBlocks, slow>>

\* Fine lock: claim a specific block, only within the zone whose token the
\* train already holds, and only up to its per-visit quota.
AcquireBlock(t, b) ==
  /\ trainToken[t] # "none"
  /\ SameZone(trainToken[t], b)
  /\ blockOcc[b] = "free"
  /\ usedBlocks[t] < MaxBlocksFor(t)
  /\ blockOcc' = [blockOcc EXCEPT ![b] = t]
  /\ trainBlocks' = [trainBlocks EXCEPT ![t] = trainBlocks[t] \cup {b}]
  /\ usedBlocks' = [usedBlocks EXCEPT ![t] = usedBlocks[t] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, trainToken, slow>>

ReleaseBlock(t, b) ==
  /\ b \in trainBlocks[t]
  /\ blockOcc[b] = t
  /\ blockOcc' = [blockOcc EXCEPT ![b] = "free"]
  /\ trainBlocks' = [trainBlocks EXCEPT ![t] = trainBlocks[t] \ {b}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, trainToken, usedBlocks, slow>>

\* Coarse unlock: only once every block it backed has been released.
ReleaseZone(t) ==
  /\ trainToken[t] # "none"
  /\ trainBlocks[t] = {}
  /\ tokenHolder' = [tokenHolder EXCEPT ![trainToken[t]] = "free"]
  /\ trainToken' = [trainToken EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
  /\ usedBlocks' = [usedBlocks EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockOcc, trainBlocks, slow>>

\* Dispatch may flag/unflag a train as running slow only between trips.
SetSlow(t) ==
  /\ ~slow[t]
  /\ trainToken[t] = "none"
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, blockOcc, trainToken, trainBlocks, usedBlocks>>

ClearSlow(t) ==
  /\ slow[t]
  /\ trainToken[t] = "none"
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, blockOcc, trainToken, trainBlocks, usedBlocks>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, tok \in Tokens : AcquireZone(t, tok)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : AcquireBlock(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : ReleaseBlock(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : ReleaseZone(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : SetSlow(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : ClearSlow(t)

ReleaseBlockStep(t) == \E b \in Blocks : ReleaseBlock(t, b)

Fairness ==
  /\ \A t \in Trains : SF_vars(ReleaseBlockStep(t))
  /\ \A t \in Trains : SF_vars(ReleaseZone(t))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: capacity conservation. Every occupied block traces back to a
\* zone token its occupant legitimately still holds -- capacity is never
\* created out of nothing nor kept alive after its authority is gone.
CapacityConservation ==
  \A b \in Blocks :
    blockOcc[b] # "free" =>
      /\ trainToken[blockOcc[b]] # "none"
      /\ SameZone(trainToken[blockOcc[b]], b)
      /\ b \in trainBlocks[blockOcc[b]]

\* LIVENESS: a train that has claimed a zone token -- slow or not -- always
\* eventually finishes its move through the zone and returns the token.
TripCompletes == \A t \in Trains : (trainToken[t] # "none") ~> (trainToken[t] = "none")

====
nl:
A metro operator runs a two-zone signalling block system on a busy line. Each
zone (zone 1 and zone 2) contains two physical track-block segments and is
protected by a coarse-grained zone-capacity token pool: two tokens per zone,
each token representing one unit of movement authority the interlocking is
willing to grant into that zone at a time. A train may not touch any block
inside a zone until it first claims one of that zone's tokens; this is the
coarse (hierarchical) lock. Once a train holds a zone token it may then claim
the fine-grained lock on individual block segments within that same zone --
never a block in the other zone, since a token only backs blocks in its own
zone. Each train is normally allowed to hold only one block segment locked at
a time inside its current zone visit, but dispatch can flag a train as
"running slow": a slow train is not failed or removed from service, it simply
moves more cautiously, so the interlocking pre-clears one extra block of
advance movement authority for it (up to two blocks per visit instead of
one) so it does not stall the corridor behind it. A train releases each block
lock as it clears that segment, and only once it holds no block locks at all
may it release its zone token back to the shared pool, freeing that unit of
capacity for another train. The slow flag itself can only be toggled between
trips, never while a train is mid-transit through a zone.

The full action set is: AcquireZone (a train claims a free zone-capacity
token, the coarse lock), AcquireBlock (a train that already holds a zone
token claims a free block segment inside that same zone, up to its quota),
ReleaseBlock (a train releases one block segment it currently holds),
ReleaseZone (a train that holds no block segments releases its zone token
back to the pool), SetSlow (dispatch flags an idle train as running slow),
and ClearSlow (dispatch clears the slow flag from an idle train).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every occupied block segment is always backed by a zone
token its occupant currently and legitimately holds for that same zone, so
movement-authority capacity is never occupied out of nothing and never left
stranded once its backing token is released.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every train that has claimed a zone token -- whether
running slow or not -- eventually releases every block segment it holds and
returns the zone token to the pool.

---- MODULE W4Od9m7p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* A power-grid load shedder: each feeder carries a compare-and-swap shed
\* register. A controller may only flip it from "armed" to "shed" -- the
\* irreversible act of dropping that feeder's load -- if the register still
\* reads "armed" at the moment of the swap (the compare). A privileged admin
\* may also perform the swap, bypassing the normal claim step that ordinary
\* controllers must go through first, but the compare against "armed" still
\* applies to everyone. The invariant guards that the irreversible shed is
\* attributed to exactly one actor and its one-shot version marker never
\* advances past the single legitimate swap.

CONSTANTS Feeders, Controllers

VARIABLES shedState, nominee, executedBy, casVersion

vars == <<shedState, nominee, executedBy, casVersion>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ shedState \in [Feeders -> {"armed", "shed"}]
  /\ nominee \in [Feeders -> Controllers \cup {"none"}]
  /\ executedBy \in [Feeders -> Controllers \cup {"admin", "none"}]
  /\ casVersion \in [Feeders -> 0..2]

Init ==
  /\ shedState = [f \in Feeders |-> "armed"]
  /\ nominee = [f \in Feeders |-> "none"]
  /\ executedBy = [f \in Feeders |-> "none"]
  /\ casVersion = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]

\* A controller claims the dispatcher's queue slot for a feeder before it may
\* attempt the compare-and-swap on it.
Nominate(c, f) ==
  /\ shedState[f] = "armed"
  /\ nominee[f] = "none"
  /\ nominee' = [nominee EXCEPT ![f] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shedState, executedBy, casVersion>>

\* A controller may back out of a claim it never acted on.
Withdraw(c, f) ==
  /\ nominee[f] = c
  /\ shedState[f] = "armed"
  /\ nominee' = [nominee EXCEPT ![f] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shedState, executedBy, casVersion>>

\* The compare-and-swap itself: compare shedState[f] against "armed", swap
\* to "shed". Only the feeder's current nominee may attempt it.
CasShed(c, f) ==
  /\ nominee[f] = c
  /\ shedState[f] = "armed"
  /\ shedState' = [shedState EXCEPT ![f] = "shed"]
  /\ executedBy' = [executedBy EXCEPT ![f] = c]
  /\ casVersion' = [casVersion EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
  /\ nominee' = [nominee EXCEPT ![f] = "none"]

\* Twist: the admin may perform the same compare-and-swap on an emergency
\* feeder without first holding the nomination -- a privileged bypass of the
\* normal claim step -- but the compare against "armed" still gates it, so
\* an already-shed feeder cannot be shed a second time even by the admin.
AdminOverrideShed(f) ==
  /\ shedState[f] = "armed"
  /\ shedState' = [shedState EXCEPT ![f] = "shed"]
  /\ executedBy' = [executedBy EXCEPT ![f] = "admin"]
  /\ casVersion' = [casVersion EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
  /\ nominee' = [nominee EXCEPT ![f] = "none"]

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, f \in Feeders : Nominate(c, f)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, f \in Feeders : Withdraw(c, f)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, f \in Feeders : CasShed(c, f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : AdminOverrideShed(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: the irreversible shed happens at most once per feeder. A feeder
\* is unattributed exactly while armed and attributed exactly once it has
\* been shed, and its CAS register advances past its single legitimate swap
\* for no feeder.
AtMostOnceShed ==
  \A f \in Feeders :
    /\ (shedState[f] = "armed") <=> (executedBy[f] = "none")
    /\ (shedState[f] = "shed") => (casVersion[f] = 1)
    /\ casVersion[f] <= 1

====
nl:
A regional power grid runs an automatic load shedder over a handful of
feeders during capacity emergencies. Each feeder carries a single
compare-and-swap register that starts "armed" and can be flipped exactly
once to "shed" -- physically dropping that feeder's load -- because
re-energizing a shed feeder requires a manual field crew visit, not a
protocol action, so within this protocol the shed is irreversible. A pool of
grid controllers coordinates who gets to pull the trigger on each feeder: a
controller first nominates itself for a feeder (claiming that feeder's
dispatcher queue slot) while the feeder is still armed and unclaimed, and
only the controller currently holding that nomination may attempt the
compare-and-swap, which compares the register against "armed" and, if it
still reads "armed", swaps it to "shed" and stamps a one-shot version marker.
A controller that no longer needs to act may withdraw its nomination while
the feeder is still armed. Because grid emergencies can outrun the normal
nomination workflow, a privileged system admin may also perform the same
compare-and-swap directly on any armed feeder without first holding its
nomination -- bypassing the claim step everyone else must go through -- but
the compare against "armed" still applies to the admin exactly as it does to
ordinary controllers, so an already-shed feeder can never be shed again, not
even by the admin override.

The full action set is: Nominate (a controller claims the dispatcher slot on
an armed, unclaimed feeder), Withdraw (a controller relinquishes a claim it
never acted on), CasShed (the holder of a feeder's nomination performs the
compare-and-swap that sheds it), and AdminOverrideShed (the privileged admin
performs the same compare-and-swap on any armed feeder, bypassing the
nomination requirement).

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every feeder, the irreversible shed action executes at
most once -- a feeder stays unattributed exactly while its register reads
"armed" and becomes attributed to exactly one actor (a controller or the
admin) exactly when it is shed, and its compare-and-swap version marker
never advances past that single legitimate swap.

---- MODULE W4Od16m5p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* A pharmacy dispenser gated by quorum voting: pharmacists cast votes for a
\* prescription over an asynchronous network modelled as a SET of in-flight
\* messages (not a queue), so delivery order need not match send order --
\* votes can be reordered or even withdrawn before they land. Dispensing the
\* prescription is irreversible and may only happen once, and only once a
\* quorum of votes has actually been delivered (not merely sent).

CONSTANTS Pharmacists, Prescriptions, Quorum

ASSUME Quorum \in Nat /\ Quorum <= Cardinality(Pharmacists)

VARIABLES network, delivered, dispensed, dispenseCount

vars == <<network, delivered, dispensed, dispenseCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ network \subseteq (Pharmacists \X Prescriptions)
  /\ delivered \subseteq (Pharmacists \X Prescriptions)
  /\ dispensed \in [Prescriptions -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ dispenseCount \in [Prescriptions -> 0..2]

Init ==
  /\ network = {}
  /\ delivered = {}
  /\ dispensed = [rx \in Prescriptions |-> FALSE]
  /\ dispenseCount = [rx \in Prescriptions |-> 0]

VotesFor(rx) == {ph \in Pharmacists : <<ph, rx>> \in delivered}

\* A pharmacist casts a vote by putting it on the network -- not yet counted.
SendVote(ph, rx) ==
  /\ <<ph, rx>> \notin network
  /\ <<ph, rx>> \notin delivered
  /\ ~dispensed[rx]
  /\ network' = network \cup {<<ph, rx>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<delivered, dispensed, dispenseCount>>

\* The network delivers some pending vote -- any one of them, not
\* necessarily the one sent earliest, which is exactly how reordering shows
\* up in this model: delivery order is a nondeterministic choice over the
\* whole in-flight set, never forced to match send order.
DeliverVote(ph, rx) ==
  /\ <<ph, rx>> \in network
  /\ network' = network \ {<<ph, rx>>}
  /\ delivered' = delivered \cup {<<ph, rx>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dispensed, dispenseCount>>

\* A pharmacist may withdraw a vote that is still in flight. Because of
\* reordering, this can race a delivery: if the network already delivered
\* the vote first, the cancel simply no longer applies.
CancelVote(ph, rx) ==
  /\ <<ph, rx>> \in network
  /\ network' = network \ {<<ph, rx>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<delivered, dispensed, dispenseCount>>

\* The irreversible dispense: fires at most once per prescription, and only
\* once a quorum of votes has actually been delivered.
Dispense(rx) ==
  /\ ~dispensed[rx]
  /\ Cardinality(VotesFor(rx)) >= Quorum
  /\ dispensed' = [dispensed EXCEPT ![rx] = TRUE]
  /\ dispenseCount' = [dispenseCount EXCEPT ![rx] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<network, delivered>>

Next ==
  \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists, rx \in Prescriptions : SendVote(ph, rx)
  \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists, rx \in Prescriptions : DeliverVote(ph, rx)
  \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists, rx \in Prescriptions : CancelVote(ph, rx)
  \/ \E rx \in Prescriptions : Dispense(rx)

Fairness == \A rx \in Prescriptions : WF_vars(Dispense(rx))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: dispensing is quorum-gated and happens at most once. Whenever a
\* prescription has been dispensed, a quorum of votes stands delivered for
\* it, the count of times it was dispensed is bounded by one, and the
\* boolean flag and the one-shot count agree with each other.
QuorumGatedOnce ==
  \A rx \in Prescriptions :
    /\ dispensed[rx] => Cardinality(VotesFor(rx)) >= Quorum
    /\ dispenseCount[rx] <= 1
    /\ dispensed[rx] <=> dispenseCount[rx] = 1

\* LIVENESS: once a prescription has actually accumulated a delivered
\* quorum -- however the reordered votes happened to land -- it is
\* eventually dispensed.
DispenseEventually ==
  \A rx \in Prescriptions :
    (Cardinality(VotesFor(rx)) >= Quorum) ~> dispensed[rx]

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Pharmacists = {ph1, ph2, ph3}
  Prescriptions = {rx1, rx2}
  Quorum = 2
INVARIANT QuorumGatedOnce
PROPERTY DispenseEventually
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital pharmacy dispenses controlled prescriptions only after a quorum
of on-duty pharmacists sign off. Each pharmacist can cast one vote per
prescription: casting a vote puts a vote message onto the pharmacy's
internal messaging network, which is asynchronous -- messages sit as an
unordered pool of in-flight votes rather than a first-in-first-out queue, so
the network is free to deliver them in any order, not necessarily the order
they were sent. A pharmacist may also withdraw a vote that is still in
flight, but because delivery order is not guaranteed, a withdrawal can lose
a race against delivery: if the network happens to deliver that vote first,
the later withdrawal simply no longer has anything to act on. Once a
prescription has accumulated a quorum of actually delivered votes (not
merely sent ones), the dispensing station may perform the dispense itself --
handing over the physical medication, which cannot be undone by any protocol
action, so it may happen at most once per prescription and only while it has
not already been dispensed.

The full action set is: SendVote (a pharmacist places a vote for a
prescription onto the in-flight network), DeliverVote (the network delivers
some pending vote -- any one of them, independent of send order, which is
how reordering shows up), CancelVote (a pharmacist withdraws a vote still in
flight, which fails if reordering already delivered it first), and Dispense
(the station irreversibly dispenses a prescription once a quorum of votes
for it has been delivered).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a prescription is dispensed at most once, only while a
quorum of votes stands delivered for it, and its dispensed flag and its
one-shot dispense count always agree with each other.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: once a prescription has actually accumulated a delivered
quorum of votes -- however the reordered messages happened to land -- it is
eventually dispensed.

---- MODULE W4Od1m0p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Runway slot allocation by optimistic locking with retry: a flight reads a
\* slot's current version, then sends a propose message carrying that
\* version over an asynchronous network. The network is modelled as a SET
\* of in-flight messages rather than a queue, so it may deliver -- or the
\* tower may garbage-collect -- proposals in any order, out of send order.
\* A proposal only commits if its carried version still matches the slot's
\* live version at processing time, which is what keeps a stale, reordered
\* proposal from ever double-allocating a slot.

CONSTANTS Flights, Slots, MaxVersion

ASSUME MaxVersion \in Nat

VARIABLES slotOwner, slotVersion, network, allocated

vars == <<slotOwner, slotVersion, network, allocated>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ slotOwner \in [Slots -> Flights \cup {"free"}]
  /\ slotVersion \in [Slots -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ network \subseteq (Flights \X Slots \X (0..MaxVersion))
  /\ allocated \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {"none"}]

Init ==
  /\ slotOwner = [s \in Slots |-> "free"]
  /\ slotVersion = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ network = {}
  /\ allocated = [f \in Flights |-> "none"]

\* Read the slot's current version and send a propose message carrying it.
\* Also how a flight retries after a failed attempt: it simply proposes
\* again, reading whatever the version happens to be now.
Propose(f, s) ==
  /\ allocated[f] = "none"
  /\ slotVersion[s] < MaxVersion
  /\ network' = network \cup {<<f, s, slotVersion[s]>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, allocated>>

\* The tower processes some pending proposal -- any one of them, chosen
\* independently of send order, which is how reordering shows up here. It
\* commits only if the carried version still matches the slot's live
\* version and the slot is still free; otherwise the optimistic lock has
\* failed and the message is simply consumed with no effect.
ProcessPropose(f, s, v) ==
  /\ <<f, s, v>> \in network
  /\ network' = network \ {<<f, s, v>>}
  /\ IF v = slotVersion[s] /\ slotOwner[s] = "free" /\ allocated[f] = "none"
     THEN /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = f]
          /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
          /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![f] = s]
     ELSE UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, allocated>>

\* The tower garbage-collects a proposal it can already tell is stale
\* (its carried version trails the slot's live version) without bothering
\* to run it through the commit check.
DropStale(f, s, v) ==
  /\ <<f, s, v>> \in network
  /\ v < slotVersion[s]
  /\ network' = network \ {<<f, s, v>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, allocated>>

\* A flight cancels and gives its runway slot back, freeing it for others.
Release(f) ==
  /\ allocated[f] # "none"
  /\ LET s == allocated[f] IN
       /\ slotVersion[s] < MaxVersion
       /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = "free"]
       /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![f] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED network

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots : Propose(f, s)
  \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots, v \in 0..MaxVersion : ProcessPropose(f, s, v)
  \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots, v \in 0..MaxVersion : DropStale(f, s, v)
  \/ \E f \in Flights : Release(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: no double allocation of the same runway slot. Whatever a flight
\* records as its held slot always agrees with the slot's own record of its
\* owner, and no two distinct flights ever record the same held slot.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  /\ \A f \in Flights : allocated[f] # "none" => slotOwner[allocated[f]] = f
  /\ \A f1, f2 \in Flights :
       (allocated[f1] # "none" /\ allocated[f1] = allocated[f2]) => f1 = f2

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Flights = {f1, f2, f3}
  Slots = {s1, s2}
  MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator hands out a small set of scheduled runway
slots to flights using optimistic locking with retry. A flight that wants a
slot reads that slot's current version number and sends a propose message
carrying the version it saw off into the tower's messaging network. That
network is asynchronous: it holds proposals as an unordered pool of
in-flight messages rather than a first-in-first-out queue, so the tower can
end up processing them in any order -- not necessarily the order in which
they were sent. When the tower processes a proposal, it commits the
allocation only if the version the message carries still matches the slot's
live version and the slot is still free; if either has changed since the
flight read it, the optimistic lock has failed and the proposal is simply
consumed with no effect, leaving the flight to retry by proposing again
against whatever version is now current. The tower may also proactively
garbage-collect a proposal it can already tell is stale -- its carried
version trailing the slot's current version -- without running it through
the commit check at all. A flight holding a slot may also cancel, releasing
it back to "free" and bumping its version so that any old, now-obsolete
proposals for it are guaranteed to fail their version check.

The full action set is: Propose (a flight reads a slot's current version and
sends a proposal carrying it, also how a flight retries after a failed
attempt), ProcessPropose (the tower processes some pending proposal, in
whatever order it happens to pick, committing it if the carried version
still matches and the slot is free, otherwise discarding it as a failed
optimistic lock), DropStale (the tower discards a proposal it can already
tell is stale without running the commit check), and Release (a flight
holding a slot cancels and frees it, advancing its version).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the same runway slot is never double-allocated -- every
flight's record of the slot it holds always agrees with that slot's own
record of its owner, and no two distinct flights ever end up recording the
same held slot.

---- MODULE W4Od17m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* An airport baggage router where two independently-operated sorter
\* instances ("A" and "B", one per terminal) share a single bounded holding
\* buffer between the belts and the loading bay. Admission and removal are
\* both governed by a compare-and-swap register (poolCount): an instance
\* reads the register, then attempts to swap it, retrying from the read if
\* the other instance's own CAS beat it to the register in between. The
\* invariant guards that the shared buffer's bound is never exceeded even
\* though both instances contend for the very same register.

CONSTANTS BagsA, BagsB, Capacity

ASSUME Capacity \in Nat

Bags == BagsA \cup BagsB
Instances == {"A", "B"}
OwnerOf(b) == IF b \in BagsA THEN "A" ELSE "B"
MaxCount == Cardinality(Bags)

VARIABLES bagState, poolCount, pendingBag, pendingSnapshot

vars == <<bagState, poolCount, pendingBag, pendingSnapshot>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ bagState \in [Bags -> {"queued", "inpool", "delivered"}]
  /\ poolCount \in 0..MaxCount
  /\ pendingBag \in [Instances -> Bags \cup {"none"}]
  /\ pendingSnapshot \in [Instances -> 0..MaxCount]

Init ==
  /\ bagState = [b \in Bags |-> "queued"]
  /\ poolCount = 0
  /\ pendingBag = [i \in Instances |-> "none"]
  /\ pendingSnapshot = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

\* Read phase for admitting a bag into the shared buffer: snapshot the
\* register before attempting the swap.
StartInsert(i, b) ==
  /\ OwnerOf(b) = i
  /\ bagState[b] = "queued"
  /\ pendingBag[i] = "none"
  /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = b]
  /\ pendingSnapshot' = [pendingSnapshot EXCEPT ![i] = poolCount]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bagState, poolCount>>

\* Swap phase: succeeds only if the register still reads what this instance
\* last saw AND there is still room under the shared cap; otherwise this is
\* a failed compare-and-swap and the instance must go back and re-read.
CasInsert(i) ==
  /\ pendingBag[i] # "none"
  /\ bagState[pendingBag[i]] = "queued"
  /\ LET b == pendingBag[i] IN
       IF poolCount = pendingSnapshot[i] /\ poolCount < Capacity
       THEN /\ poolCount' = poolCount + 1
            /\ bagState' = [bagState EXCEPT ![b] = "inpool"]
            /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
            /\ UNCHANGED pendingSnapshot
       ELSE /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<poolCount, bagState, pendingSnapshot>>

\* Read phase for handing a bag out of the shared buffer to its terminal.
StartRemove(i, b) ==
  /\ OwnerOf(b) = i
  /\ bagState[b] = "inpool"
  /\ pendingBag[i] = "none"
  /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = b]
  /\ pendingSnapshot' = [pendingSnapshot EXCEPT ![i] = poolCount]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bagState, poolCount>>

\* Swap phase for removal: same compare-and-swap discipline, freeing one
\* unit of shared capacity on success.
CasRemove(i) ==
  /\ pendingBag[i] # "none"
  /\ bagState[pendingBag[i]] = "inpool"
  /\ LET b == pendingBag[i] IN
       IF poolCount = pendingSnapshot[i]
       THEN /\ poolCount' = poolCount - 1
            /\ bagState' = [bagState EXCEPT ![b] = "delivered"]
            /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
            /\ UNCHANGED pendingSnapshot
       ELSE /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<poolCount, bagState, pendingSnapshot>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Bags : StartInsert(i, b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : CasInsert(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Bags : StartRemove(i, b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : CasRemove(i)

Fairness ==
  \A i \in Instances :
    /\ SF_vars(\E b \in Bags : StartInsert(i, b))
    /\ SF_vars(CasInsert(i))
    /\ SF_vars(\E b \in Bags : StartRemove(i, b))
    /\ SF_vars(CasRemove(i))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: the shared buffer's bound is never exceeded by either instance's
\* traffic, even though both contend for the same compare-and-swap register.
BoundedCapacity == poolCount <= Capacity

\* LIVENESS: every bag either instance queues eventually gets all the way
\* through the shared buffer and out, regardless of how the two instances'
\* compare-and-swap attempts interleave and race on the shared register.
BagDelivered == \A b \in Bags : (bagState[b] = "queued") ~> (bagState[b] = "delivered")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  BagsA = {a1, a2}
  BagsB = {b1, b2}
  Capacity = 2
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
PROPERTY BagDelivered
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport runs two independently operated baggage-sorter instances, one
serving Terminal A's belts and one serving Terminal B's, but both funnel
bags through a single shared holding buffer between the sorters and the
loading bay -- the two instances are otherwise completely independent, they
just happen to share this one pool of buffer capacity. Admission to and
removal from the shared buffer are both governed by a single compare-and-swap
register that holds the current occupancy count. To admit one of its own
bags, an instance first reads the register's current value, then attempts to
swap it to one higher; the swap only succeeds if the register still holds
the value the instance last read and there is still room under the shared
cap, otherwise the compare-and-swap has failed (the other instance's own
traffic changed the register in between) and the instance must go back and
re-read before trying again. Removing a bag from the buffer once it reaches
its own terminal works the same way in reverse: read the register, then
attempt to swap it one lower, retrying on failure. Because both instances
hit the very same register, an admission by one and a removal by the other
can interleave in any order, and the compare-and-swap discipline is what
keeps the shared buffer's bound safe despite that contention.

The full action set is: StartInsert (an instance snapshots the register
before trying to admit one of its own queued bags), CasInsert (the instance
attempts the compare-and-swap that admits the bag, succeeding only if the
register still matches its snapshot and there is room, otherwise failing and
forcing a retry), StartRemove (an instance snapshots the register before
trying to hand off one of its own buffered bags), and CasRemove (the
instance attempts the compare-and-swap that removes the bag, succeeding only
if the register still matches its snapshot).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared buffer's bound is never exceeded, no matter how
the two instances' compare-and-swap attempts on the one shared register
interleave.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bag either instance queues into the shared buffer
is eventually delivered all the way through and out, regardless of how the
two instances' compare-and-swap retries race against each other.
